sections.title: The letter di
paragraphs: The letter is called (di) /di/. Its sound is a consonant, which blocks the air in the mouth. You hear it in the word (dove) /ˈdo.ve/, which means where. This letter has only one sound in Italian.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Place the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper front teeth. It is a dental consonant, meaning you make it with the teeth. Stop the air for a moment. Then let the air burst out. Turn your voice on so your throat vibrates. Put a hand on your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always keeps the same sound. In all positions, it sounds like the start of (dente) /ˈdɛn.te/. You hear the very same sound inside the word (cadere) /kaˈde.re/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make this sound on the gum ridge behind your teeth, like in door. Place your tongue tip directly on the back of your upper front teeth instead.
